alt: Slide 1 of 7. Your retirement savings, in five steps. 1952 to 2023
Slide 2 of 7. OAS, 1952. Old Age Security. A basic pension for older Canadians. Today it is the base layer many retirement incomes start from.
Slide 3 of 7. RRSP, 1957. Registered Retirement Savings Plan. A tax break for people with no workplace pension. Today it is one common way to build the private layer.
Slide 4 of 7. CPP, 1966. Canada Pension Plan. A pension earned through work and contributions. Today it adds a layer that follows a person's work history.
Slide 5 of 7. TFSA, 2009. Tax-Free Savings Account. Savings that grow without tax on the growth. Today it is a flexible place to save beside the RRSP.
Slide 6 of 7. FHSA, 2023. First Home Savings Account. In law: after March 2023. Savings aimed at a first home. Today it is the newest account, built for one goal.

Slide 7 of 7. Every date, checked at its official source. OAS 1952: Office of the Chief Actuary, OSFI. RRSP 1957: Statistics Canada. CPP 1966: Office of the Chief Actuary, OSFI. TFSA 2009: Justice Laws Website. FHSA 2023: Justice Laws Website. Made with AI assistance. I directed and reviewed the work and checked every figure against its source. Education only, not advice.
